solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tool, rasp initially wrapped in cloth

indicators.note: the rasp's first letter is enclosed by the cloth word, as if swaddled

parts.note: a towel is a cloth for drying

indicators.note: initially asks for just the opening letter of rasp

explanation.surface: A rasp is found bundled up in a piece of cloth in the toolbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand implement used by gardeners and bricklayers, so it is a kind of tool.

clue.text: I'm great playing this style of piano music

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of I'm great are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A pianist boasting about how good they are at this music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated American piano style associated with Scott Joplin.

clue.text: Complaining cry from first of holidaymakers entering Bordeaux?

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Bordeaux is a French wine, so it stands for wine

indicators.note: first of picks the initial letter of holidaymakers

explanation.surface: A tourist arriving in the French city of Bordeaux is grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bordeaux?' looks like the place, but the question mark tells you it is the wine from there.
explanation.definitionFit: A whine is a high-pitched complaining sound or a peevish grumble.

clue.text: To calm down, use lift at college

parts.note: to lighten is to lift, as a mood or load is lightened
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student is told to relax by taking the elevator at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like an elevator; here it is the verb meaning to make lighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to relax and stop being so serious is telling them to calm down.

clue.text: Confront eccentric king, perhaps

parts.note: to face someone is to confront them
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: Standing up to an odd monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of playing cards the king is one of the picture cards, alongside queen and jack.

clue.text: Highwayman may make one pay for protection

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
a pad is protective padding, as worn by cricketers

explanation.surface: A robber who extorts payment in return for safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpad was a robber of travellers who went on foot rather than mounted, a sort of highwayman.

clue.text: Seat I must sit in daily

indicators.note: sitting in something puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a daily is a British charwoman or cleaner, also called a char

explanation.surface: Someone being told to take their usual seat every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily, in Britain, is a cleaner who comes in each day; CHAR is short for charwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a single seat with a back for one person.

clue.text: Brief conversation in support of bridge puzzle

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece beneath supports the piece above it

parts.note: to cross is to span or bridge something
a word is a brief talk, as in 'a word in your ear'

explanation.surface: A quick chat while playing the card game bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' looks like the card game, but it is the verb meaning to span.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword is a word puzzle in a grid, an example of a puzzle.

clue.text: Large number, nearly all in administration

indicators.note: nearly all means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a regiment can mean a large number or multitude

explanation.surface: Lots of people almost entirely working in government.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a regulated system of management or government, an old sense of administration.

clue.text: Fetching article, number costing much less than it should

definitions.text: costing much less than it should

parts.note: going for something is fetching it, as in going for help
a is the indefinite article
a number is a song in a show or set

explanation.surface: An attractive piece of writing and a tune that both turn out to be bargains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' looks like an adjective meaning attractive; here it is the verb, to go and get.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sold for a trifling price is said, idiomatically, to change hands for next to nothing.

clue.text: Find a way around spin and pace

parts.note: side is spin put on a ball in snooker or billiards
a step is a single pace

explanation.surface: Advice to a bowler or dancer on getting past an obstacle with spin and speed.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE for spin is a British cue-sports term for the spin imparted by striking the ball off-centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid a problem by moving around it is to dodge it, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Continue to imagine parking's not available

indicators.note: something not available is absent, so the parking letter is removed

parts.note: to presume is to suppose or imagine
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone carries on supposing they will find a space though the car park is full.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up again after a pause is to carry on, so the verb means continue.

clue.text: Not as busy in class?

parts.note: less means not as much, so 'not as' busy is less busy
on means engaged or in operation, as a busy line is on

explanation.surface: A question about whether a classroom is quieter than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a period of teaching, as is a class at school.

clue.text: He'd put in cryptic clues and grid, finally programmed

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside another
cryptic means puzzling, so the letters of clues are mixed up
finally takes only the last letter of grid

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the letters as written

explanation.surface: A setter describing how they inserted their own touch into the clues and grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' looks like a description of the clues themselves, but it is the anagram signal; the apostrophe in He'd is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scheduled has been timetabled in advance, just as broadcasts are programmed.

clue.text: Ignore reduction

definitions.meaning: to disregard something as not worth considering
a cut in the price of goods

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to dismiss a possibility; the noun is money knocked off the asking price.

clue.text: Unpalatable character interrupting lecture?

indicators.note: interrupting means one piece breaks into another

parts.note: to scold is to lecture someone
tone is character or quality, as in the tone of a place

explanation.surface: A disagreeable person heckling a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person, but it is tone, meaning quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Food served stone cold, when it should be hot, is unappetising and unpalatable.

clue.text: On a trip, identify most memorable moment

parts.note: someone on a drug trip is high
to spot something is to pick it out or identify it

explanation.surface: Picking out the best moment of a holiday journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a trip' reads as travel, but it means intoxicated by drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The best or most exciting part of an event is its highlight or peak.

clue.text: Disinclination to act shown by one with damaged retina

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters of retina are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with an eye problem is unwilling to do anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to do nothing or to resist change, a lack of motivation.

clue.text: Left over in seaport abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something remained behind in a foreign harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything remaining in excess, with some to spare, is surplus or left over.

clue.text: Being out-of-date, this should not be worn at Ladies' Day!

definitions.text: this should not be worn at Ladies' Day!
definitions.meaning: Ladies' Day at Royal Ascot is a British race day famous for extravagant new hats, so an aged one would be out of place

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stale or familiar, and literally names worn headwear unfit for a fashion-conscious racecourse.

clue.text: Made up of famous people, the whole side originally on pitch

parts.note: all means the whole of something

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of side

parts.note: pitch is the black sticky substance tar

explanation.surface: An entire team of celebrities first lining up on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a playing field, but it is the substance tar.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-star cast or team consists entirely of celebrated performers.

clue.text: Head croupier's left to trade with diamonds

indicators.note: the letter for left swaps places with the letter for diamonds, as if trading

parts.note: a croupier deals cards at a casino table, so is a dealer

explanation.surface: A casino croupier has gone off to do business in gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is L and 'diamonds' (the card suit) is D; in DEALER these two letters swap places, making DEAL into LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader is the person in charge, the chief or head of a group.

clue.text: Lover of chrome, oddly

indicators.note: of shows the answer is made from part of the next words

explanation.surface: Someone fond of shiny chrome, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like an instruction to take odd letters, but the answer runs across chrome and oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo, Shakespeare's young hero, gives his name to any ardent male lover.

clue.text: Start to suggest leaving out sinister controller

indicators.note: the start of suggest is just its first letter
out signals the letters of leaving are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone begins to hint that they are leaving the evil mastermind's service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving out' looks like an instruction to omit letters; in fact 'out' rearranges LEAVING into VENGALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby, gives his name to anyone who manipulates another malevolently.

clue.text: Rise and dress

definitions.meaning: to get out of bed in the morning, phrased as two words
an outfit, especially an elaborate or odd one

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to stand or rise from bed; hyphenated, the noun is an outfit or costume.

clue.text: I know I want you to advise me on computers and stuff

definitions.meaning: a weary agreement that one has had the same experience

definitions.text: I want you to advise me on computers and stuff
definitions.meaning: a literal request to be informed on a subject such as IT

explanation.definitionFit: Used idiomatically it is rueful agreement; taken literally it asks someone to explain a topic to you.

clue.text: Husband, even more generous

parts.note: 'and some' is a colloquial phrase meaning and even more besides

explanation.surface: A spouse who becomes more generous still.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum or gift is a large, liberal one, so the word can mean generous.

clue.text: Leave extremely disreputable character

indicators.note: the extremes of disreputable are its first and last letters

parts.note: a part is a character or role in a play

explanation.surface: A shady figure being told to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go away from a place, which is to leave it.
